findings.where: Article specimen, the pull quote “Whichever PPP Law I am currently working on with a client country!” (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The pull quote is set in the logo blue. The tile's own palette gives that blue to the wordmark, links and the button. Here it colours text that does nothing, and it sits a few lines above a real blue link. Set in italic at display size, it reads as a link or a highlighted action.
findings.who_objects: An official skimming one of Mark's articles would click the quote expecting a source or a related piece, and nothing would happen. Angélique, who will copy this look when she adds posts, would learn that blue can mean either a link or emphasis.

findings.where: First screen, desktop and phone: the hero heading, standfirst and 'Get in touch'
findings.fault: The tile does not answer the 'calm first' value. The heading, the claim and the button are all there at first paint, and the motion sketch only lifts the heading into place in 580 ms. Nothing quiet comes before the ask. Under this direction's own card, the built mark or Mark himself would be that moment, and the tile does not show where it goes.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for one quiet moving picture or moment before any text asks for anything. Round 2 and the animation round (#9) would also have no guidance from this direction on where that moment sits.

findings.where: First screen, the standfirst ('Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience') and the hero as a whole
findings.fault: The only standing shown beside the action is a size word and one past title. The first screen names no region of his work and no recent work, article or talk. The newest piece appears only as a specimen far below.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank official chooses an advisor by relevant work and region, against terms of reference. 'Over 40 years' gives them nothing to check before they write. They want to know that he has done PPP law work for bodies like theirs, in their region.

findings.where: First screen, 'Get in touch' (mailto:) and the nav's 'Contact'; the page has no footer
findings.fault: The email address is never shown as text. The only route is a mailto button, which fails silently on a machine with no mail client set up. The nav's 'Contact' goes nowhere, and the page ends with no footer carrying the address or a contact route.
findings.who_objects: An official on a locked-down bank workstation or webmail clicks 'Get in touch', no window opens, and they have no address to copy into their own mail. The one action this site exists for is lost.

findings.where: Nav bar, 'Articles' and 'Blog' side by side (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: Two of the four nav labels name what a visitor takes to be the same thing. Nothing tells them which holds Mark's PPP writing, and the specimen page's 'MMM Infra Blog No. 8' only blurs the line further.
findings.who_objects: An official looking for Mark's published thinking on PPP law has to guess, and may open both. The nav's job is to save them that.

findings.fault: 'Play again' is a button that replays the animation in place, but it wears the underlined blue link style, which the palette keeps for links. It looks like it will take the visitor to another page.
findings.who_objects: Round 2's designer, who takes the tile as the system: they would read an underlined blue phrase as both a link and an in-page action, so the two functions share one look.

findings.where: Motion sketch, the heading 'precise, light, quick'
findings.fault: This heading is set large in Source Sans 3 semibold. The tile's own type pair says Source Sans is for the nav, buttons, labels and dates only, with Gelasio for headings. The tile breaks its own type rule.
findings.who_objects: Round 2's designer and Angélique, who will follow the tile. It shows two contradictory heading voices and does not say which one is the rule.

findings.where: Style tile section labels: 'Texture' and 'Motion sketch' have a hairline under them; 'Palette', 'Type pair' and 'An article page' do not
findings.fault: Labels at the same level get two different treatments, depending on the column they sit in, so a reader cannot tell which treatment is the house's.
findings.who_objects: Round 2's designer, who draws section headings from this tile. Two treatments for one kind of label leave the system unclear.

findings.where: Apostrophes in 'World Bank's' (hero standfirst), 'The World's Best' (article heading) and 'Georgia's' (type-pair note)
findings.fault: The apostrophes are straight typewriter marks, while the article beside them uses curly quotes (“ ”). At display size in a Georgia-style serif, the straight mark stands out.
findings.who_objects: A senior legal reader, who is used to properly set text. A straight apostrophe in the hero and in an article headline looks unfinished in a look that sells care and judgement.
